# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

## Native pages (pages the design package doesn't include)
- Author in the package's own format under `tools/nxm/native/<slug>/`: `body.html` (with `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{FOOTER}}`), `page.css`, `page.js`, `meta.json` (`title`, `description`, `anchors`, `assets`). `port_pages.py` assembles them exactly like the package's `build_page.py` (shared shell + common.css + Aurora + your css/js) and runs the same pipeline. Add the slug to `ROUTES` in `nxmlib.py` (or a fan-out in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`).
- Free tools: `native/tools` (hub) and `native/tools-app` (every tool page, routes/tools-app.json); `native/tools-tool` is the original template, kept unchanged for the skin creator only. See docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "Free tools overhaul".
- Reference implementations: `native/about` (story + liquid-glass photo + real product prices), `native/security` (diagram + card grids + the Compare page's disclosure board), `native/affiliate` (data-driven promo), `native/legal` (article reading layout, 4 routes from one template).
- Write markup with the DESIGN's classes (`au-btn`, `au-btn--glass`, `au-card`, `au-glass`, `h2pill`, `gp-head`, `h2`, `lede`, `section`, `container`, `faq-wrap`/`faq`, `wh-final`, `data-au-icon="…" data-grad`) — the porter maps buttons to the library hierarchy. Links to other pages as `https://nxeon.cloud/<route>` (the porter makes them relative / keeps ported ones inside /nxm).
- Pure-copy pages: a wire module with `STATIC = True` and no loader.
- Body attributes: `<body class="pg-x" style="--acc:…" data-…>` land on the page wrapper; `.pg-x …` selectors are rewritten to match it.
- Loader extras: `trail` (breadcrumb below Home when ancestors aren't in the registry), `particles` (per-item colours), `crumb`.
- Interactive React pieces (e.g. a live tool component) can be mounted into a slot element with a small client component + `createPortal` — see `app/nxm/_components/HeroParticles.tsx`.
- SEO for new routes: add an entry to `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts` (title/description/crumb) or return them from `meta(p)`.
- The box is also production: keep Playwright runs sequential (one browser at a time) and don't restart the shared dev server (:3033, 4 GB heap cap).

# ── native pages: pages the design package doesn't include ─────────────────
# Authored in the package's own page format (body.html with {{SPRITE}}/{{NAV}}/
# {{FOOTER}}, page.css, page.js, meta.json) under tools/nxm/native/<slug>/ and
# assembled exactly like the package's build_page.py: shared shell + common.css
# + aurora + the page's own css/js. Then the same pipeline as every page.
NATIVE = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/native"
def build_native(slug):
    D = f"{NATIVE}/{slug}/"
    meta = json.load(open(D + "meta.json"))
    p1, p2, p3 = (open(f"{SRC}/part{i}.html").read() for i in (1, 2, 3))
    MAIN = "https://claude.ai/artifact/KryegJ1sG3zYzX7MyxypYs"
    head = re.sub(r"<title>.*?</title>", f"<title>{meta['title']}</title>", p1, count=1)
    head = re.sub(r'<meta name="description" content="[^"]*">', f'<meta name="description" content="{meta["description"]}">', head, count=1)
    head = head.replace('url("__IMG_HERO2__")', "none").replace('url("__IMG_GRAIN__")', "none")
    css = open(f"{SRC}/pages/common.css").read() + AURORA_CSS + (open(D + "page.css").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.css") else "")
    head = head.replace("</style>", css + "</style>", 1)
    sprite = p2[p2.index("<body>") + 6:p2.index("</svg>") + 6]
    local = set(meta.get("anchors", []))
    def fix_links(h):
        h = re.sub(r'href="#([a-z-]*)"', lambda m: f'href="#{m.group(1)}"' if (m.group(1) in local or m.group(1).startswith("i-")) else f'href="{MAIN}#{m.group(1)}"', h)
        return h.replace(f'href="{MAIN}#top"', f'href="{MAIN}"')
    nav = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<a class="skip"'):p2.index("</header>") + 9]).replace(f'href="{MAIN}#main"', 'href="#main"')
    nav = nav.replace('<a class="logo" href="#top"', f'<a class="logo" href="{MAIN}"')
    footer = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<footer class="footer"'):p2.index("</footer>") + 9])
    body = open(D + "body.html").read()
    for k, v in {"SPRITE": sprite, "NAV": nav, "FOOTER": footer, "MAIN": MAIN}.items():
        body = body.replace("{{" + k + "}}", v)
    helpers = p3[p3.index("<script>"):p3.index("/* ------------------------------------------------------------------")]
    def blk(a, b): i = p3.index(a); j = p3.index(b, i + len(a)); return p3[i:j]
    js = helpers + "document.getElementById('year') && (document.getElementById('year').textContent = new Date().getFullYear());\n"
    js += blk("/* ============ Navigation ============ */", "/* ============ Reveal, rules")
    js += blk("/* ============ Reveal, rules, in-view hooks, counters ============ */", "/* ============ Hero: Power Your")
    js += AURORA_JS + "\n" + (open(D + "page.js").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.js") else "") + "\n})();\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n"
    html = head + body + js
    A = f"{PKG}/assets/"
    m = {k: (v if v.startswith("/") else A + v) for k, v in meta.get("assets", {}).items()}
    m.setdefault("LOGO", A + "logo.png")
    for _k in ["minecraft", "rust", "palworld", "valheim", "ark", "cs2"]:
        m.setdefault("NAV_" + _k.upper(), A + "nav/" + _k + ".webp")
    mime = lambda q: "image/png" if q.endswith(".png") else "image/svg+xml" if q.endswith(".svg") else "image/jpeg" if q.endswith(".jpg") else "image/webp"
    for k in sorted(m, key=len, reverse=True):
        html = html.replace(f"__IMG_{k}__", f"data:{mime(m[k])};base64," + _fake_b64(open(m[k], "rb").read()).decode())
    left = set(re.findall(r"__IMG_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__", html)); assert not left, left
    return html

EXT = {"image/png": "png", "image/webp": "webp", "image/jpeg": "jpg", "image/svg+xml": "svg", "image/gif": "gif"}
def externalise(s):
    def rep(m):
        h = m.group(2); ext = EXT.get(m.group(1), "bin")
        path = f"{ASSET_DIR}/{h}.{ext}"
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            open(path, "wb").write(_blobs[h])
        return f"/nxm/a/{h}.{ext}"
    s = re.sub(r"data:([\w/+.-]+);base64,NXMA([0-9a-f]{16})", rep, s)
    assert "NXMA" not in s
    return s

AURORA_CSS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.css").read()
AURORA_JS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.built.js").read()

def port(slug):
    html = externalise(build_native(slug) if os.path.isdir(f"{NATIVE}/{slug}") else build(slug))
    head, rest = html.split("</head>", 1)
    title = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", head).group(1)
    desc_m = re.search(r'<meta name="description" content="([^"]*)"', head)
    desc = desc_m.group(1) if desc_m else ""

    # CSS: the page's one stylesheet minus Aurora (already loaded, scoped, by
    # app/nxm/layout.tsx), scoped under this page's wrapper.
    css = re.search(r"<style>([\s\S]*)</style>", head).group(1)
    assert AURORA_CSS in css, "aurora.css not found verbatim"
    css = geist(css.replace(AURORA_CSS, ""))
    scope, rootcls = f".nxm-p-{slug}", f":root.nxm-p-{slug}-root"
    # the design's <body …>: its classes, CSS variables and data-* move to the
    # page wrapper (a nested page can't touch <body>); `xray` is a class the
    # design's JS toggles on body
    btag = re.search(r"<body([^>]*)>", html).group(1)
    battr = lambda n: (re.search(rf'{n}="([^"]*)"', btag) or [None, ""])[1]
    bclasses = battr("class").split()
    body_attrs = {"cls": " ".join(bclasses), "style": battr("style"),
                  "data": {k: v for k, v in re.findall(r'data-([\w-]+)="([^"]*)"', btag)}}
    hoisted, rules = scope_css(css, scope, rootcls, frozenset(bclasses) | {"xray"})
    extra = (f"\n{scope}{{{FONT_VARS}}}\n"
             f"{rootcls}{{--nav-h:68px;background:#060913}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta:only-child{{grid-column:1/-1}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nxm-navcta{{white-space:nowrap}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta{{height:48px;justify-content:center;font-size:1rem}}\n"
             f"@media (max-width:1080px){{{scope} .nv-act>.nxm-navcta{{display:none}}}}\n")
    css_out = ("/* GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py from the design package — do not edit. */\n"
               + "\n".join(hoisted) + "\n" + "\n".join(rules) + extra)

    # Markup: everything between <body> and the page script.
    js_at = rest.rfind("<script>")
    body, js = rest[:js_at], rest[js_at:]
    body = re.sub(r"^\s*<body[^>]*>", "", body.strip())
    body = relink(body)
    for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []):
        assert old in body, (slug, old); body = body.replace(old, new)
    body, btns = swap_buttons(body)
    body, nrev = reviews_slot(body)
    body, ncta, nlogin, npost = nav_slots(body)
    assert ncta == 2 and nlogin == 2 and npost == 1, (slug, ncta, nlogin, npost)
    body, nfoot = re.subn(r'<footer class="footer"[\s\S]*?</footer>', "", body)
    assert nfoot == 1, (slug, nfoot)
    body = re.sub(r"<!--(?!NXM:)[\s\S]*?-->", "", body)
    stray = balanced(body)
    assert not stray, f"{slug}: stray end tags {stray[:3]}"
    wire = load_wire(slug)
    if wire and hasattr(wire, "body"):
        body = wire.body(body)

    # Script: the page's JS minus the Aurora runtime (mounted once by the layout).
    js = re.search(r"<script>([\s\S]*)</script>", js).group(1)
    assert AURORA_JS in js, "aurora.built.js not found verbatim"
    js = js.replace(AURORA_JS, "")
    js = js.replace("https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js", "/nxm/three.min.js")
    # body attributes now live on the page wrapper
    js = js.replace("document.body.dataset", "document.querySelector('.nxm-p').dataset")
    js = js.replace("document.body.classList.toggle('xray'", "document.querySelector('.nxm-p').classList.toggle('xray'")
    js = relink(js)
    for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []):
        js = js.replace(old, new)
    js = js_buttons(js)
    if wire and hasattr(wire, "js"):
        js = "var __NXM = JSON.parse((document.getElementById('nxm-data') || {}).textContent || 'null');\n" + wire.js(js)
    # Money in the visitor's display currency (NxmPage emits #nxm-fx): the same
    # rules as the live site's convertAndFormat; USD keeps the design's "$12.99".
    js = js.replace("'$' + Math.round(v).toLocaleString('en-US')", "__nxmMoney(Math.round(v), 0)")
    js = re.sub(r"'\$' \+ v\.toLocaleString\('en-US'(?:, \{[^}]*\})?\)", "__nxmMoney(v)", js)
    js = js.replace("'$' + v.toFixed(2)", "__nxmMoney(v)")
    assert "'$' +" not in js, f"{slug}: unconverted '$' + … money formatting in the page script"
    js = FX_PRELUDE + js
    assert "cdnjs" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in body
    stale = audit(slug, body, js, getattr(wire, "ALLOW", set()) if wire else set())
    STATUS[slug] = ("static (no system data)" if (wire is not None and getattr(wire, "STATIC", False)) else "wired" if wire else "NOT WIRED") + (f", stale {stale}" if stale else "")

    d = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/{slug}"; os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    open(f"{d}/page.css", "w").write(css_out)
    open(f"{d}/content.ts", "w").write(
        "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. Trusted, static markup\n"
        "// from the owner's own design package (never user input).\n"
        f"export const TITLE = {json.dumps(title)};\n"
        f"export const DESCRIPTION = {json.dumps(desc)};\n"
        f"export const BODY_HTML = {json.dumps(body)};\n"
        f"export const BODY_ATTRS = {json.dumps(body_attrs)};\n")
    open(f"{d}/script.ts", "w").write(
        "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. The page's own script.\n"
        f"export const PAGE_SCRIPT = {json.dumps(js)};\n")

    route = ROUTES[slug]
    loader = wire is not None and os.path.exists(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts")
    static = bool(wire is not None and getattr(wire, "STATIC", False))
    assert wire is None or loader or static, f"{slug}: wire module without app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts"
    has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read()
    for r, fixed in routes_for(slug):
        if ("[" in r or fixed) and not has_meta:
            STATUS[slug] = STATUS.get(slug, "") + f" (route {r} not written: template needs its loader)"
            continue
        write_route(slug, r, fixed, loader)
    print(f"{slug:36} {BASE}{route if route != '/' else ''}  css {len(css_out)//1024}KB  body {len(body)//1024}KB  "
          f"js {len(js)//1024}KB  buttons {btns}  reviews {nrev}")
    return slug

# ── routes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A page is a TEMPLATE when its route has [params] (e.g. /mods/[family]/[slug])
# or when tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json fans it out to many fixed routes
# (e.g. the game template -> /rust-server-hosting {family: "rust"}, ...).
# Loaders get the params: load(p) / meta(p).
def routes_for(slug):
    f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/routes/{slug}.json"
    if os.path.exists(f):
        return [(e["route"], e.get("params", {})) for e in json.load(open(f))]
    return [(ROUTES[slug], {})]

def write_route(slug, route, fixed, loader):
    """One route file. Every route passes its [params], fixed template params
    and ?query (search, pagination, ?topic= deep links…) into the loader as one
    map; the concrete path (/mods/[family]/[slug] -> /mods/minecraft/lithium)
    is used for canonical and breadcrumbs."""
    rd = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm{route}"; os.makedirs(rd, exist_ok=True)
    rel = os.path.relpath(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm", rd)
    pc = PARTICLES.get(slug)
    particles = f' particles={{{{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}}}' if pc else ""
    # loader-supplied colours (e.g. per game) win over the slug default
    pdefault = f' ?? {{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}' if pc else ""
    has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read()
    dyn = "[" in route
    assert not (dyn or fixed) or has_meta, f"{slug}: template routes need a loader with meta(p) for SEO"
    path_expr = ("`" + re.sub(r"\[(\w+)\]", r"${p.\1}", route) + "`") if dyn else json.dumps(route)
    if loader:
        imp = (f'import {{ load{", meta" if has_meta else ""} }} from "{rel}/_data/{slug}";\n'
               f'import type {{ NxmLoad }} from "{rel}/_data/lib";\n'
               f'import {{ nxmParams }} from "{rel}/_data/params";\n')
        ptype = "{ params: Promise<Record<string, string>>; searchParams: Promise<Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>> }"
        getp = f"const p = await nxmParams(params, searchParams, {json.dumps(fixed)});"
        metacall = f"nxmMetadata({path_expr}, await meta(p))" if has_meta else f"nxmMetadata({path_expr})"
        body = f"""export async function generateMetadata({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}): Promise<Metadata> {{
  {getp}
  return {metacall};
}}

export default async function Page({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}) {{
  {getp}
  const d: NxmLoad = await load(p);
  return <NxmPage slug="{slug}" route={{{path_expr}}} body={{C.BODY_HTML}} attrs={{C.BODY_ATTRS}} particles={{d.particles{pdefault}}} slots={{d.slots}} data={{d.data}} jsonLd={{d.jsonLd}} crumb={{d.crumb}} trail={{d.trail}} />;
}}"""
    else:
        imp = ""
        body = f"""export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {{
  return nxmMetadata({path_expr});
}}

export default async function Page() {{
  return <NxmPage slug="{slug}" route={{{path_expr}}} body={{C.BODY_HTML}} attrs={{C.BODY_ATTRS}}{particles} />;
}}"""
    open(f"{rd}/page.tsx", "w").write(f"""// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit.
import type {{ Metadata }} from "next";
import {{ NxmPage }} from "{rel}/_components/NxmPage";
import {{ nxmMetadata }} from "{rel}/_seo/meta";
import * as C from "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/content";
{imp}import "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/page.css";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
{body}
""")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    slugs = sys.argv[1:] or [s for s in ROUTES if s != "home"]
    for s in slugs:
        port(s)
    # the client runtime imports each page's script by slug
    keys = sorted(os.listdir(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages"))
    open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/scripts.ts", "w").write(
        "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit.\n"
        "// Each page's script is its own chunk, loaded only on that page.\n"
        "export const SCRIPTS: Record<string, () => Promise<{ PAGE_SCRIPT: string }>> = {\n"
        + "".join(f'  {json.dumps(k)}: () => import("./{k}/script"),\n' for k in keys if os.path.isdir(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/{k}"))
        + "};\n")
    print("\nreal-data audit (launch needs every page 'wired' with no stale prices):")
    for k, v in STATUS.items():
        print(f"  {k:36} {v}")
    print("assets:", len(os.listdir(ASSET_DIR)), "files,",
          sum(os.path.getsize(f"{ASSET_DIR}/{f}") for f in os.listdir(ASSET_DIR)) // 1024 // 1024, "MB")

import { SPR, APP } from "@/lib/nx/sprites";
import { NX_ICONS, NX_ICON_TONE, type NxTone } from "@/lib/nx/icon-paths";

/* ── one dial for icon size, site-wide ────────────────────────────────────
   Every mark in the system is drawn a fixed multiple of the size its call site
   asks for. Applying it HERE rather than editing hundreds of call sites keeps
   the relative sizing intact: an icon that was deliberately smaller than its
   neighbour stays proportionally smaller, it is just bigger in absolute terms.
   Change this one number to retune the whole set.

   Note for anyone adding a primitive: scale exactly ONCE per rendered mark.
   `Plate` draws an `Icon` inside itself, so it scales its own BOX and passes
   the raw size through — scaling in both places would compound to 2.25x. */
export const ICON_SCALE = 1.5;
export const iconPx = (n: number) => Math.round(n * ICON_SCALE);

/**
 * One interface mark.
 *
 * VECTOR FIRST, sprite as the fallback. `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts` carries the set
 * redrawn as 24x24 paths; anything it defines renders as an inline SVG in
 * `currentColor`, and anything it doesn't — the sheet's brand row (linux,
 * docker, postgres…) and the five 3D product renders — still comes off
 * `public/nx/nxicons.webp` exactly as before.
 *
 * Why the switch is here rather than at 137 call sites: the sprite's marks are
 * pre-coloured, so one inside a tinted control renders in the SHEET's colour
 * instead of the control's (a teal shieldcheck on a violet "Admin" chip is the
 * bug that started this). Routing both through one component means every call
 * site gets `currentColor` without being edited, and a name with no vector yet
 * silently keeps working.
 *
 * `size` still means what it always did — ICON_SCALE is applied here for BOTH
 * paths, so a swap is 1:1 and `Plate` (which sizes its box with `iconPx`)
 * needs no change.
 */
export function Icon({
  name, size = 20, className = "", style, strokeWidth = 1.8, tone,
}: {
  name: string; size?: number; className?: string; style?: React.CSSProperties;

content.content:
/**
 * The Nexion interface set, redrawn as vector paths.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS. The original set ships as one raster sheet
 * (public/nx/nxicons.webp, mapped by lib/nx/sprites.ts) where every mark is
 * pre-coloured, pre-glowed art. That is fine as decoration and wrong as an
 * icon system: a sprite cannot take `currentColor`, so a mark inside a tinted
 * control renders in the sheet's colour rather than the control's. That bit
 * for real on the Team page's role chips — the sheet's shieldcheck is teal,
 * so the violet "Admin" chip got a teal mark.
 *
 * These are single-colour outlines on a 24x24 grid with a 1.8 stroke, rounded
 * caps and joins. NO GLOW, deliberately: glow is a property of the place a
 * mark is used (a chip, a stat tile, a nav rail), so it belongs to that
 * component's CSS — a drop-shadow baked into 100 icons cannot be turned off
 * where it isn't wanted, and cannot follow the tone of whatever contains it.
 *
 * Keys match lib/nx/sprites.ts exactly, so `<NxIcon name="crown" />` and
 * `<Icon name="crown" />` name the same mark and a call site can move over
 * one at a time.
 *
 * NOT redrawn, on purpose:
 *   - Row 6 of the sheet (windows, linux, ubuntu, apple, docker, postgres…).
 *     Those are third-party BRAND marks; hand-approximating a trademark is
 *     both worse-looking and not ours to redraw. BillingView already pulls
 *     real brand geometry from simple-icons (CC0) — same answer here.
 *   - nlogo3d / earth3d / shield3d / layers3d / chatsupport. Those are 3D
 *     product renders, not line icons; flattening them to outlines throws
 *     away the whole point of them. They stay raster art.
 */

#!/bin/bash
# Usage: dev-run.sh <command...>   (runs INSIDE the shared build lock)
# Starts the worktree dev server on :3077, runs the command, kills the server by its own PID.
cd /tank/nxeon-wt-baremetal || exit 1
nice -n 15 ionice -c3 env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 ./node_modules/.bin/next dev -p 3077 > /root/agent-notes/bare-metal/dev.log 2>&1 &
PID=$!
for i in $(seq 1 90); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://localhost:3077/api/health && break; sleep 1; done
"$@"; RC=$?
kill $PID 2>/dev/null; sleep 2; kill -9 $PID 2>/dev/null
# next dev forks a child server; kill any child of our PID tree still on the port
P=$(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | awk '/:3077 /{print $NF}' | grep -o 'pid=[0-9]*' | cut -d= -f2 | head -1); [ -n "$P" ] && kill $P 2>/dev/null
exit $RC
#!/bin/bash
# One locked session: warm the routes, time them, shoot every step, kill the server.
cd /tank/nxeon-wt-baremetal
/root/agent-notes/bare-metal/time-routes.sh /dashboard/dedicated "/dashboard/dedicated?build=$(cat /root/agent-notes/bare-metal/.cfgid)" /dashboard/dedicated/cmuwwblpk0004hl8ibg87ndmy /dashboard/services /dedicated-servers /dedicated-servers/singapore > /root/agent-notes/bare-metal/timings-after.txt 2>&1
nice -n 15 node /root/agent-notes/bare-metal/shoot.mjs > /root/agent-notes/bare-metal/shoot.log 2>&1
nice -n 15 node /root/agent-notes/bare-metal/stripe-test.mjs > /root/agent-notes/bare-metal/stripe.log 2>&1

model DedicatedCatalogItem {
  id                   String   @id @default(cuid())
  /// Upstream subsidiary the prices are for (e.g. "WE").
  subsidiary           String
  /// eco | baremetalServers (which public catalogue the plan came from).
  catalog              String
  /// Upstream plan code (ADMIN-ONLY). Regional variants are separate plans.
  planCode             String
  productCode          String
  /// kimsufi | soyoustart | rise | advance | game | scale | hgr | other
  range                String
  /// Upstream commercial name (ADMIN-ONLY, e.g. "ADVANCE-1").
  name                 String
  invoiceName          String
  cpuBrand             String
  cpuModel             String
  cpuCount             Int      @default(1)
  cpuCores             Int
  cpuThreads           Int
  cpuFrequencyGhz      Float?
  cpuBoostGhz          Float?
  defaultRamGb         Int?
  defaultStorage       String?
  defaultBandwidthMbps Int?
  /// Upstream datacenter codes this plan can be ordered in.
  datacenters          String[]
  currency             String
  /// Upstream monthly price (no commitment) + list setup fee, in cents.
  monthlyCents         Int
  setupCents           Int
  /// Setup after a live upstream promotion, null when none.
  promoSetupCents      Int?
  /// [{mode, months, termCents, setupCents}] commitment terms.
  terms                Json
  promotions           Json
  releaseYear          Int?
  slaPercent           Float?
  antiDdos             String?
  spec                 Json
  /// sha256 of the parsed item, to count real changes per sync.
  hash                 String

  // ---- Nxeon controls (never overwritten by a sync) ----
  /// Shown in customer catalogue. Default hidden: the owner opts items in.
  visible              Boolean  @default(false)
  /// Admin pin for the customer "Most popular" tag (lib/dedicated/tags.ts). Additive, 2026-10-07.
  popularPinned        Boolean  @default(false)
  /// Nxeon customer-facing name ("Nx Metal 6"); blank = generated from specs.
  displayName          String   @default("")
  markupPercent        Float?
  markupFixedCents     Int?
  overrideMonthlyCents Int?
  /// pass | waived | custom ; null = global default.
  setupPolicy          String?
  setupCustomCents     Int?
  /// Nxeon region codes hidden for this item only.
  hiddenRegions        String[] @default([])
  adminNote            String   @default("")

  firstSeenAt          DateTime @default(now())
  lastSeenAt           DateTime @default(now())
  /// Set when the plan disappears upstream (kept for history/offers, never deleted).
  removedAt            DateTime?
  priceChangedAt       DateTime?
  previousMonthlyCents Int?
  updatedAt            DateTime @updatedAt
  options              DedicatedCatalogOption[]

  @@unique([subsidiary, planCode])
  @@index([range])
  @@index([visible, removedAt])
}
model DedicatedCatalogOption {
  id            String               @id @default(cuid())
  itemId        String
  item          DedicatedCatalogItem @relation(fields: [itemId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  /// memory | storage | system-storage | bandwidth | vrack | gpu
  family        String
  planCode      String
  /// Upstream product code — joins DedicatedAvailability.memory/storage.
  productCode   String
  label         String
  isDefault     Boolean              @default(false)
  mandatory     Boolean              @default(false)
  monthlyCents  Int
  setupCents    Int                  @default(0)
  ramGb         Int?
  storageGb     Int?
  bandwidthMbps Int?
  trafficTb     Float?
  spec          Json
  lastSeenAt    DateTime             @default(now())
  removedAt     DateTime?

  @@unique([itemId, planCode])
  @@index([family])
}
model DedicatedAvailability {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  /// API host group the feed came from ("ca" | "eu" | "us").
  feed          String
  planCode      String
  fqn           String
  memory        String?
  storage       String?
  systemStorage String?
  datacenter    String
  /// 1H-high | 1H-low | 24H | 72H | 240H | 480H | comingSoon | unavailable | unknown
  availability  String
  fetchedAt     DateTime

  @@unique([feed, fqn, datacenter])
  @@index([planCode])
}
model DedicatedCatalogSync {
  id               String    @id @default(cuid())
  /// worker | admin | script
  trigger          String
  subsidiary       String
  /// RUNNING | OK | PARTIAL | FAILED
  status           String    @default("RUNNING")
  startedAt        DateTime  @default(now())
  finishedAt       DateTime?
  durationMs       Int?
  plansSeen        Int       @default(0)
  added            Int       @default(0)
  changed          Int       @default(0)
  removed          Int       @default(0)
  priceChanges     Int       @default(0)
  optionsSeen      Int       @default(0)
  availabilityRows Int       @default(0)
  /// Per-catalogue counts + ranges + datacenters seen, for the admin panel.
  summary          Json?
  warnings         Json?
  error            String?
  requestedById    String?

  @@index([startedAt])
}

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac

I'm sketching the SVG helper function that builds either stroke-based outline icons or filled icons depending on the icon type, for use on both the server and client sides.

Now I'm drafting the hero section markup for body.html, including the background sky image with fade overlay, the title and lede text, call-to-action buttons, a lineup list showing three server size tiers with images and core-count labels, and a stats definition list.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

That would explain revealed items appearing blank even though the scroll loop should have triggered them earlier. I should write a quick debug script to count how many `.dd-rv` elements have the `.in` class after settling, to confirm this theory.

## Bare metal marketing v2: report

The redesign is built and committed on `feature/bm-v2-marketing` in `/tank/dev-worktrees/bm-v2-mkt`. Nothing is merged or deployed. `devhost tsc` is clean. The dedicated tests are 78 of 89 passing. The 3 failures happen when the tests import `lib/geo-ip.ts`: it throws a `server-only` error at import, and I did not touch that file or anything it pulls in. The screenshots pass with no horizontal scroll at 390 and 1440 and no page errors. One console 503 shows up for a single resource in the dev environment, which I did not trace.

### Commits
- `a430532600` — the redesign
- `34457d528a` — polish after the first screenshot pass
- `461f822be5` — fixed-width flag column in the list view

### Files changed
- **Hand-edited source:**
  - `tools/nxm/native/dedicated-servers/body.html`
  - `tools/nxm/native/dedicated-servers/page.css`
  - `tools/nxm/native/dedicated-servers/page.js`
  - `tools/nxm/native/dedicated-servers/meta.json` (new `hardware` anchor)
- **Regenerated with `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py dedicated-servers`** (audit says "wired"):
  - `app/nxm/_pages/dedicated-servers/{content.ts,page.css,script.ts}`
  - dedicated-servers is still a generated native page. Edit the `native/` files and regenerate; never hand-edit `_pages/`. A regenerate does not undo this work.
- **Loader:** `app/nxm/_data/dedicated-servers.ts`
  - New slots for the hero copy, the hardware section title and the hardware tiles.
  - Each card carries its class tint and its size render (from `size-tier.ts`).
  - The portal's own icon paths are sent once in the page data.
  - The gate, noindex, JSON-LD and buy links are unchanged.
- The country route, the generator and the portal files were not touched. Country pages work (`/dedicated-servers/canada` returns 200; a country with no stock returns 404).

### What was built
- **Hero (concept B):** centred, with the aurora-arc plate behind it and the three renders standing small to large. The live stats sit on a thin line underneath. For SEO the H1 is "Bare metal dedicated servers" as a small kicker, then "A whole server. Nobody else on it."
- **New hardware section:** AMD, Intel and NVIDIA in large glass tiles. Every figure is computed from the in-stock catalogue: number of builds, max cores, the from price, and which classes use that maker. The NVIDIA tile only appears when a GPU build is listed. Each tile filters the catalogue to that maker.
- **Filter:**
  - Card view (concept A): class tiles with live counts, location chips with flags, processor logo toggles, four range sliders.
  - List view (concept D): the same filter becomes a sticky left rail with checkboxes, beside rows that have a coloured class edge and the size render.
  - On phones the panel folds behind a "Filters" button.
- **Card:** built to the shared spec and matched to the portal's in-progress styles in `bm.css`. It uses the same class tints as the portal (Core cyan, Pulse magenta, Forge violet, Titan blue, GPU lime).
- **Effects:** a one-time 12px fade-up as sections and cards enter, a one-time staggered rise for the hero renders, hover lifts, and a 64-second plate drift. All motion is off under reduced motion; I checked that in Playwright.
- **Fix:** the class icons were silently blank before, because the old icon names "blade" and "spark" don't exist.

### How to view it
The page is gated. I seeded my own throwaway node-2 database with 13 fake builds and turned on `dedicated_public_enabled` there; no production data was used. The seed and Playwright scripts are untracked in `.bmv2/` inside the worktree and are not committed. To view it: `devhost dev` from the worktree, then open `/nxm/dedicated-servers` (I set `NXEON_ENV=staging` with `devhost env set`). All dev servers are stopped; the worktree and its node-2 copy are left in place.

### Screenshots
In `/root/agent-notes/bm-v2-marketing/` (`-d` = 1440 desktop, `-m` = 390 phone):
- `hero-d.jpg`, `hero-m.jpg`
- `infrastructure-d.jpg`, `infrastructure-m.jpg`
- `filter-cards-d.jpg`, `filter-cards-m.jpg`
- `cards-d.jpg`, `cards-m.jpg`, `card-hover-d.jpg`
- `list-d.jpg`, `list-m.jpg`
- `full-d.jpg`, `full-m.jpg`

### What got in the way
- Nothing was denied by the permission system.
- node-2's agent memory cap (7 GB) was used up for about 30 minutes by the other session's two dev servers, so my first page compile stalled. A production release build also ran in the middle of my work. I stopped my own dev server both times and waited rather than compete.

### Decisions for the owner and the portal session
1. **AMD logo:** the only AMD logo on the site (`public/nxm/home/logos-amd.svg`) is the Ryzen mark. It appears next to EPYC builds on cards, in the filter and on the AMD tile, both here and in the portal's `BrandLogo`. The owner did ask for "Ryzen" logos, but an EPYC build under a Ryzen mark comes close to the "don't call EPYC Ryzen" rule. Should we get a plain AMD logo (and maybe an EPYC one) for EPYC builds?
2. **Headline:** I used "A whole server. Nobody else on it." as the owner picked, replacing "Bare metal dedicated servers. Yours alone." The keyword is kept inside the H1 as the kicker. Is that acceptable for SEO?
3. **"Talk to us"** (from concept B) now replaces the old "Bare metal or VPS?" button and links to `/contact`.
4. **Captions under the hero renders** ("Under 8 cores", "8 to 23 cores", "24+ cores or a GPU") come from the real size-tier rules. Keep them, or drop them for an even quieter hero?
5. **For the portal session:** `aurora-veil.webp` has a bright speck at its top-right edge that shows in every card's art area. I crop it out here (the plate is 118% tall, anchored at the bottom); the portal's `.bm-well-plate` will show it unless it does the same.
6. `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` was not updated; it is outside the files this task covered.

21032:## Bare Metal portal v2 (2026-10-08, branch `feature/bm-v2`)
## Bare Metal portal v2 (2026-10-08, branch `feature/bm-v2`)

The owner picked pieces from four concepts rendered in the real app (review page: claude.ai artifact "Bare Metal Concepts").

- **Size renders.** The owner's 1-, 3- and 5-unit NX server renders live in `public/nx/art/bm/tier-{1,2,3}.webp`. They share one 711px transparent canvas, bottom-aligned, so equal display boxes keep their true relative size. `lib/dedicated/size-tier.ts` maps a build to a size: 24+ cores or a GPU = 3, 8 to 23 cores = 2, fewer = 1. The portal catalogue, My Services and the marketing page all use it, so a build gets the same picture everywhere.
- **Hero** (`components/dedicated/flow/CatalogueHero.tsx`): aurora-veil plate, the small/medium/large lineup (real per-size core range and from-price), and the AMD, Intel and NVIDIA marks (NVIDIA only when a GPU build is listed). It is `nx-dark-island`, so it stays dark in the light theme.
- **Catalogue** (`components/dedicated/flow/Catalogue.tsx`):
  - One toolbar holds search, sort, reset and the Cards/List toggle.
  - Cards view: class tiles with in-stock counts, then location chips, processor logos and range sliders.
  - List view: the same filters in a left rail beside rows with a class-colour edge and the size render.
  - The card has an art well (plate + class glow + size render), glass tags and the name on the art, and one mini-card per spec. The storage headline shows the total, with the drive layout in the sub-line.
- **Tags** (`.bm-tag` in `components/dedicated/bm.css`): glass pills with a per-kind colour and icon. The light theme off the art uses a pale tint with dark ink.
- **Palette.** `bm.css` dark tokens moved from graphite to the portal's navy (`--bm-line` = rim-hi, cards use the service-card gradient), so bare metal no longer looks like a separate product.
- **My Services.** `ServiceRow.bareMetal` (`lib/nx/services.ts`) carries cpu/cores/RAM/storage. `ServiceCard` draws the size render on the aurora plate and adds Cores/Memory/Storage tiles. There is no usage data for bare metal, so no usage bars are shown.
- **Gotcha.** `.bm-btn-ghost` (unlayered CSS) beats Tailwind's `lg:hidden` on the same element. Put responsive visibility on a wrapper.

## Renewal analytics — /admin/analytics/renewals (2026-10-07, branch `fix/portal-batch-2026-10-07`)

Admin page (area `analytics`, `requireArea("analytics")`) under Growth → Traffic & analytics → **Renewals**, also linked from `/admin/analytics` and the footer of `/admin/reports`. Read-only; no schema change. Code: `lib/renewal-analytics.ts` (server-only DB loader), `lib/renewal-analytics-core.ts` (pure classification + math, tested in `test/renewal-analytics.test.ts`), `app/admin/analytics/renewals/page.tsx`.

**Who counts.** Real customers only, via the reports' `realUser()` SQL (`lib/reports/sql.ts`): role CUSTOMER, `excludeFromRevenue = false`, no internal QA e-mail suffix. Services whose owner account was deleted are dropped (cannot be verified). Free servers (`isFree`) and partner-granted servers (`PartnerGrant` not `CONVERTED`) are excluded — they are never billed.

**The unit: a renewal cycle** = (service, due date). Products: VPS, game server (`Server`, renewed by `worker/billing.ts`), web hosting (`HostingAccount`), business email (`EmailSubscription`), block storage (`Volume`) — all three by `worker/product-renewals.ts` — and domains (`Domain`, `domainAutoRenewSweep` + `renewDomainAction`). Each cycle gets one outcome:

| Outcome | Exactly what marks it |
|---|---|
| **renewed** | AuditLog `billing.renewed` (server: detail = server id, written inside `commitRenewal`, which the sweep, admin "Renew now" and the unpaid auto-recovery all use; hosting/email/volume: detail `"<kind> <id> <name> $X -> date"`), or `server.renew_now` (customer button). Joined to its PAID invoice (`Renewal:…`, `Web Hosting renewal:…`, `Business Email renewal:…`, `Block storage renewal:…`) within 20 s for the amount and `periodStart` (= due date). Domains: WalletTransaction `Domain renewal: <name> …` debits. *Recovered* = paid after a failed attempt in the same period; *early* = paid > 1 day before due (all admin Renew-now renewals so far). Source = admin when an `admin.renew_now … renewed via …` row follows within 15 s. |
| **failed** (involuntary churn) | Auto-renew was ON at the due date and the money never arrived: `billing.suspended_unpaid` / `billing.terminated_unpaid`, or a removed service whose last period had a failed charge (`billing.card_declined`, `billing.card_unusable_grace`, `admin.renew_now … FAILED — insufficientFunds`), or a live one still unpaid > 14 days after due. Rail = card if any card failure, else wallet. |
| **voluntary** churn | Auto-renew OFF at the due date (state reconstructed from `server.autorenew_toggle` / `server.cancel_period_end` history, else the row's flag), or the customer removed it: `server.delete`, `server.cancel_immediate`, `hosting.cancel`, a cancelled email sub; or the service vanished with no failed charge (incl. no removal record at all). |
| **admin** (removed by Nxeon) | `admin.fraud_teardown`, `billing.reaped_suspended` (ABUSE/ADMIN suspension), `server.cancel_immediate` with an "admin cleanup/teardown" note, `qa.sweep_teardown`. Excluded from every rate. |
| **pending** | Due date passed, nothing collected, not suspended, ≤ 14 days (dunning / card-readd grace). |

The public `/dedicated-servers` page (NXM site) and its country pages `/dedicated-servers/<country>`, rebuilt from the owner's concept picks so they match the portal (see "Bare Metal portal v2" above).

- **Where the code is.** It is a *native* NXM page. Never hand-edit the generated `app/nxm/_pages/dedicated-servers/{content.ts,page.css,script.ts}`. The loader is `app/nxm/_data/dedicated-servers.ts` (hand-written). The country route `app/nxm/dedicated-servers/[country]/page.tsx` reuses the same body and loader. The gate, noindex and sitemap rules are unchanged (`lib/dedicated/gate.ts`).
- **Slots the loader fills** (all from the in-stock catalogue, `loadOrderCatalog`, nothing invented):
  - `eyebrow`: the H1 kicker; it keeps "Bare metal dedicated servers [in <country>]" inside the H1 for SEO.
  - `h1:html`, `lede`: the lede names only the CPU lines that are in stock.
  - `count`, `from`, `maxCores`, `regions`.
  - `lineup:html`: the hero's four CPU sizes (`SIZE_TIERS`/`SIZE_NAME`), each captioned with its real core range and from-price among CPU-only builds, or "None in stock right now".
  - `infraTitle`, `infra:html`: the AMD/Intel/NVIDIA tiles. Each shows builds in stock, max cores, from-price and the classes using that maker. NVIDIA appears only when a GPU build is listed.
  - `gpuSizes:html`, `gpuAction:html`, `gpuState`: the GPU band.
  - `families:html`, `locations:html`, `countries:html`, `catTitle`, `register`.
  - `__NXM` page data also carries every card, including its `art` (`buildArt()`), its class `tint` (same `FAMILY_TINT` as the portal) and the icon paths (`lib/nx/icon-paths.ts`).
- **GPU band** (mirrors `components/dedicated/flow/GpuBand.tsx`):
  - It is always shown, even with no GPU build in the catalogue.
  - Content: the five GPU renders (`GPU_TIERS`, labels `GPU_TIER_LABEL`), each with "from $X" or "Sold out".
  - In stock: a "See N GPU builds" button filters the catalogue to NX-GPU.
  - Sold out: an amber "Currently sold out" pill and a notify form that POSTs `{kind:"gpu", email}` to `/api/dedicated/stock-alert`. A signed-in visitor gets no email field, because the API uses the account email. Success and the API's own error text (400/404/429) show inline.
- **Build card:** the shared portal spec (art well, glass tags, name on the art, one mini-card per spec). The render box is `min(42%, 190px)` and the title block stops at `right: 45%`, so the name never touches the render, even for the full-width Ultra/GPU renders. The `aurora-veil` plate is bottom-anchored at 118% so the speck at its top edge is cropped.
- **Filters:** class tiles with live counts, location chips, processor logos and sliders over the grid (cards view). The list view turns the same panel into a sticky left rail, beside rows with a class-colour edge. On phones the panel folds behind a "Filters" button. The view choice is remembered in `localStorage` (`bm-view`).
- **Effects** (owner: restrained, never "tacky"). Only these:
  - A one-time 12px fade-up for `.dd-rv` elements and the first batch of cards, staggered 50ms (IntersectionObserver; filter changes swap instantly).
  - A one-time staggered rise of the hero renders.
  - Hover lifts on the renders (6px) and cards (2px, render scale 1.03).
  - A 64s drift of the hero aurora plate.
  - Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` none of it runs: no `dd-anim` class, so nothing is ever hidden, no animations and no hover transforms. Animations use `backwards` fill only, so hover transforms are never blocked.
- **Seeing it in dev:** the page is gated and needs catalogue rows. Seed a throwaway node-2 DB (`devhost db push`, then a script that writes `Setting dedicated_public_enabled=true` plus a few `DedicatedCatalogItem`/`DedicatedCatalogOption`/`DedicatedAvailability` rows), set `devhost env set NXEON_ENV=staging`, then `devhost dev` and open `/nxm/dedicated-servers`. In Playwright, scroll with `behavior: "instant"`: the site sets smooth scrolling, so plain `scrollTo` steps never reach the bottom and the reveal never triggers.

'''
s=s[:j]+sec+s[j:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

## Bare metal marketing v2, round 2: report

All six follow-up items are done and committed on `feature/bm-v2-marketing` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/bm-v2-mkt`). `devhost tsc` is clean (exit 0). Nothing is deployed or merged to main. My dev servers are stopped; nothing of mine is running on node-2.

### Commits
- `8e430a4120` — merge of `feature/bm-v2`, including `2d61824884`. It merged cleanly and did not touch any marketing files.
- `f187b98488` — the round-2 work.

### What changed
- **Hero:**
  - Four renders in a row: Small, Medium, Large and Ultra, at their true relative size.
  - Each caption is the size name plus the real "N–M cores · from $X" from in-stock CPU-only builds, or "None in stock right now".
- **GPU section:**
  - It sits right after the hardware showcase and mirrors the portal's GPU band, with the copy as specified.
  - The five GPU renders show "from $X" or "Sold out". Sizes with nothing in stock are dimmed.
  - When GPU builds are in stock, a "See N GPU builds" button filters the catalogue to NX-GPU.
  - When none are in stock, it shows the amber "Currently sold out" pill and the email form, which POSTs to `/api/dedicated/stock-alert`. Signed-in visitors get no email field, since the API uses their account email.
  - The success line and the API's own error text show inline.
  - The section is always shown, even when the catalogue has no GPU builds at all.
- **Card renders** now come from `buildArt()`, so GPU builds get the GPU set.
- **Card title fix:**
  - The render box is now at most 42% of the art area's width (190px cap), and the title block stops at 45% from the right.
  - I measured the gap between the text and the drawn edge of the render on all 16 cards. The narrowest gaps are 8px at 1440 and 1280, 61px at 1024 and 20px at 390; the closest card is the Ultra one.
  - The renders on 3-column cards are a bit smaller than the original spec as a result.
- **Docs:** a new "Bare Metal marketing page v2" section in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, right after "Bare Metal portal v2". It covers the native files, the regenerate command, the slots, the effects and reduced-motion rule, the GPU section and stock alerts, and how to see the gated page in dev.
- The AMD/Ryzen logo is left as is.

### Files
- `tools/nxm/native/dedicated-servers/{body.html,page.css,page.js,meta.json}`
- `app/nxm/_data/dedicated-servers.ts`
- `app/nxm/_pages/dedicated-servers/*` (regenerated; the audit says "wired")
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`

### Verified (Playwright on node-2, against my throwaway DB)
- I seeded both states: 16 fake builds including a 64-core build and GPU builds with 1, 2 and 4 GPUs, then the same builds with GPU stock set to unavailable. I pushed the schema first, so the new stock-alert table exists there.
- The GPU button filters to 3 of 16 builds with NX-GPU selected.
- Submitting an empty email shows "Enter a valid email address."
- A simulated 429 from the API shows its own error text inline.
- A real POST to the throwaway DB shows "You're on the list. We'll email owner@example.com when GPU servers are back in stock."
- No horizontal scroll at 1440, 1280, 1024 or 390.

### Screenshots (`/root/agent-notes/bm-v2-marketing/round2/`)
- Hero: `hero-d.jpg`, `hero-m.jpg`
- GPU in stock: `gpu-instock-d.jpg`, `gpu-instock-m.jpg`
- GPU sold out: `gpu-soldout-d.jpg`, `gpu-soldout-m.jpg`
- Notify form states (extra): `gpu-soldout-error-d.jpg`, `gpu-soldout-done-d.jpg`
- Cards: `cards-d-1440.jpg`, `cards-d-1280.jpg`, `cards-d-1024.jpg` (extra), `cards-m.jpg`

### Notes
- The seed and shoot scripts are untracked in `.bmv2/` and not committed.
- The 3 dedicated tests that fail when they import `lib/geo-ip.ts` (from round 1) were not re-run this round.
